question: What materials are modern contraceptive diaphragms usually made of?
explanation: Modern diaphragms use soft, flexible silicone or latex so they can comfortably bend and fit inside the vagina. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h1)

question: Why do women need to use chemical spermicide along with a diaphragm?

options.A: To lubricate the device for easy insertion
options.B: To immobilize and kill sperm that pass the barrier
options.C: To permanently alter the pH of the cervix
options.D: To prevent the growth of yeast infections

explanation: While the physical cup blocks most sperm, spermicide acts as a backup to kill any little swimmers that might slip past the edges! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h1)

question: Which type of diaphragm bends easily in half along a central hinge to make putting it in easier?
explanation: An arcing spring diaphragm folds right in half like a taco, which helps guide it smoothly into place over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h2)

question: What is a big perk of the newer, single-size silicone diaphragms?

options.A: They can be left in place inside the vagina for up to a week
options.B: They do not require an internal pelvic exam for professional sizing
options.C: They completely eliminate the need to use spermicide creams
options.D: They provide full protection against all sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Universal single-size diaphragms are a lifesaver because one standard size fits most women, saving them from a traditional fitting exam. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h2)

question: During a traditional diaphragm fitting, what two points does the nurse measure between?

options.B: Posterior fornix to the pubic bone
options.C: Cervical os to the vaginal introitus
options.D: Uterine fundus to the pelvic inlet

explanation: To get the right size, clinicians measure from the back of the vagina (posterior fornix) to the back of the pubic bone. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h3)

question: A patient comes back to the clinic after losing 15 kg. What should you do as her nurse?

options.A: Instruct the client to continue using her current diaphragm device
options.B: Perform a repeat pelvic measurement for a new diaphragm size
options.C: Advise the client to stop using spermicide during intercourse
options.D: Recommend switching immediately to an oral contraceptive pill

explanation: Major weight changes shift body fat and pelvic tone, meaning she will likely need a new size for a snug, safe fit. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h3)

question: When putting in a diaphragm correctly, where should the front edge be tucked?
explanation: The front rim needs to hook securely behind the pubic bone so it stays locked tightly over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h4)

question: Why should a user hold their diaphragm up to the light before using it?

options.A: To check for small tears or holes that would let sperm pass through
options.B: To ensure the correct color coding for the specific menstrual cycle
options.C: To activate the chemical properties of the embedded spermicide
options.D: To warm up the silicone material for more comfortable insertion

explanation: A quick visual check against the light helps catch tiny punctures before they lead to an unplanned pregnancy. Simple and smart! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h4)

question: At least how long must a diaphragm stay in after sex?
explanation: Leaving it in for at least 6 hours gives the spermicide enough time to completely immobilize and destroy all viable sperm. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h5)

question: What should a client do if she has sex again just four hours after putting in her diaphragm?

options.A: Apply more spermicide into the vagina without removing the diaphragm
options.B: Remove the diaphragm immediately and use an emergency oral contraceptive
options.C: Leave everything alone because the original spermicide is still active
options.D: Take the diaphragm out, wash it, and reinsert it with fresh spermicide

explanation: For repeat intercourse, she should just push more spermicide straight into the vagina without taking the device out. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h5)

question: Which type of lubricant can damage and weaken a latex diaphragm?
explanation: Oils and petroleum jelly break down latex rubber super fast, creating weak spots and tears. Always stick to water-based lubes! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: How should a washed diaphragm be stored after it dries?

options.A: In its designated storage case away from heat and sunlight
options.B: Wrapped tightly in a plastic bag inside the kitchen freezer
options.C: At the bottom of a handbag without any protective covering
options.D: Hanging openly on a bathroom wall hook exposed to light

explanation: Keeping it in its cool, dark storage case protects the material from heat and sunlight, helping it last a long time. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: Leaving a diaphragm in for way too long can put a patient at risk for which rare, serious condition?
explanation: Keeping barrier methods in past the 24-hour mark lets bacteria multiply rapidly, raising the risk of Toxic Shock Syndrome. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h7)

question: Why do some women who use diaphragms experience more frequent urinary tract infections (UTIs)?

options.A: The spermicide alters the normal bacterial balance inside the urinary bladder
options.B: The device prevents regular urination while it is worn during the day
options.C: The silicone material absorbs urine and introduces bacteria into the kidneys
options.D: The rim of the device can press against the urethra and block complete bladder emptying

explanation: The diaphragm rim can put slight pressure on the urethra, making it harder to empty the bladder completely and causing UTIs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h7)
